newsitem.title: CHINA: China grain demand could hit 726 mln T in 2030.
newsitem.headline: China grain demand could hit 726 mln T in 2030.

text.p: Grain demand in China could hit 726 million tonnes by the year 2030 and Beijing will have to invest billions of dollars to boost yields if it wants to be mostly self-sufficient, a senior economist said on Thursday.

China could produce 663 million tonnes of grain a year by 2030 if it could boost yields by one percent a year on 110 million hectares of land, said Ma Xiaohe, an official of the Institute of Economics under the State Planning Commission.
Grain demand would be at least 633 million tonnes and could reach as high as 726 million tonnes a year by that time, Ma said in an article in the China Daily.

"China should prioritise self-reliance, while at the same time not exclude itself from the world market," Ma said, adding that imports could be as much as 100 million tonnes a year in the next century.

China would need to invest 740 billion yuan ($89 billion) to raise output on 60 million hectares of low-yield land, develop 14 million hectares of waste land, and expand irrigated land by 17 million hectares, he said.
China was facing a shortage of arable land, with total area of 95 million hectares of land under grain in 1995, down from 112 million hectares in 1957, he said.

"Perhaps China's most daunting challenge is the reduction of arable land," he said. Foreign analysts have said China's official statistics could underestimate arable land by as much as one-third, and such an error would make per-hectare yields appear higher than the real figure.
China should also cut down on the waste of grain, he said.
"On average, each year 45 billion kg of grain is wasted in transport or thrown away after produced as food," he said.
China said earlier this week it estimated the summer grain harvest at a record 118 million tonnes, up 3.5 percent compared with last year.
China reported a record harvest of 490 million tonnes last year and has said it hopes to repeat that this year.
